title: IARC marks Liver Cancer Awareness Month 2026 - International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC)

analysis.time: The event is marked on 1 October 2026, with a webinar scheduled for 14 October 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: Global, with specific mention of Asia having the highest incidence of liver cancer and Oceania having the lowest.
analysis.event: IARC marks Liver Cancer Awareness Month 2026, highlighting the global burden of liver cancer and the role of hepatitis viruses in its development.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: In 2024, almost 850,000 people developed liver cancer, and more than 730,000 died from it. Hepatitis B virus infection is estimated to have caused about 520,000 cases of liver cancer in 2024.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: IARC scientists will lead a webinar on 14 October 2026 to discuss research priorities for liver cancer prevention. The information is based on the most recent global cancer burden estimates.

analysis.brief_en: The International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) marks Liver Cancer Awareness Month 2026, highlighting the global burden of liver cancer. According to the most recent estimates, almost 850,000 people developed liver cancer in 2024, with over 730,000 deaths recorded. The IARC report emphasizes that infection with hepatitis B virus is a major contributor, with an estimated 520,000 cases linked to it. The agency also notes that liver cancer is the seventh most common cancer type worldwide and the third most common cause of cancer death. IARC scientists will host a webinar on 14 October 2026 to discuss research priorities for liver cancer prevention, focusing on evidence gaps and pressing issues in control. The event is part of broader efforts to raise awareness and promote effective prevention strategies, including vaccination programs against hepatitis B.
analysis.summary_en: The International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) marks Liver Cancer Awareness Month 2026, highlighting the global burden of liver cancer. According to the most recent estimates, almost 850,000 people developed liver cancer in 2024, with over 730,000 deaths recorded. The IARC report emphasizes that infection with hepatitis B virus is a major contributor, with an estimated 520,000 cases linked to it. The agency also notes that liver cancer is the seventh most common cancer type worldwide and the third most common cause of cancer death. IARC scientists will host a webinar on 14 October 2026 to discuss research priorities for liver cancer prevention, focusing on evidence gaps and pressing issues in control. The event is part of broader efforts to raise awareness and promote effective prevention strategies, including vaccination programs against hepatitis B.

title: Living with chronic hepatitis B in Kenya - Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance

analysis.time: The article discusses Melvin Onyango's experience with chronic hepatitis B over the past six years (N50) and mentions the national prevalence rate of hepatitis B in Kenya as of the time of the report (N18). It also references the introduction of the hepatitis B vaccine in Kenya in the early 1980s and its incorporation into the EPI in 2002 (N32).
analysis.location_and_population: The article focuses on Muhuru Bay, a town in Migori County, Kenya, which is located on the shores of Lake Victoria (N1). It also mentions the broader context of Kenya, where the national hepatitis B prevalence rate is 3.5%, and Migori County has a prevalence rate of 10% to 13% (N18).
analysis.event: The article describes Melvin Onyango's personal experience with chronic hepatitis B, which he attributes to unsafe sexual networks and the local transactional system of 'sex for fish' (N7). It also highlights the challenges in diagnosing and treating hepatitis B in Kenya, including the lack of awareness and the high prevalence rate (N18, N21).
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Approximately 1.56 million people are living with hepatitis B in Kenya, but less than 10% are diagnosed (N28). Only about 22% of those diagnosed are on proper treatment (N31). The article notes that hepatitis B can be 100 times more infectious than HIV (N27) and that it is a major cause of liver cancer and cirrhosis (N19).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The article states that the government is working on raising public awareness and plans to establish a dedicated hepatitis B research and treatment centre in Marigat, Baringo County (N26). It also mentions that targeted routine screening and expanded adult vaccination are recommended (N41). However, the article acknowledges that many rural and lower-tier facilities miss hepatitis B diagnoses (N10).

analysis.brief_en: The article discusses the prevalence and challenges of hepatitis B in Kenya, focusing on Muhuru Bay in Migori County. Melvin Onyango, a resident of the area, attributes his chronic hepatitis B infection to unsafe sexual networks and the local 'sex for fish' transactional system. The article highlights that Kenya has a national hepatitis B prevalence rate of 3.5%, with Migori County reporting 10% to 13%. It notes that the virus is highly infectious, up to 100 times more than HIV, and is a significant cause of liver cancer and cirrhosis. Despite the availability of vaccines and treatments, only 10% of those infected are diagnosed, and 22% of diagnosed individuals are on proper treatment. The government is working on public awareness campaigns and plans to establish a dedicated hepatitis B research and treatment centre in Baringo County. The article also emphasizes the importance of targeted screening and adult vaccination in combating the disease.
